question: It takes Mary \(30\) minutes to walk uphill \(1\) km from her home to school, but it takes her only \(10\) minutes to walk from school to home along the same route. What is her average speed, in km/hr, for the round trip?
solution:
Average speed is total distance divided by total time. The same route is \(1\) km each way, so Mary's round-trip distance is \(2\) km. Her total walking time is
\[
30+10=40\text{ minutes}=\frac{40}{60}=\frac23\text{ hour}.
\]
Thus her average speed is
\[
\frac{2}{2/3}=3\text{ km/hr}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{3\text{ km/hr}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
